text: You senseless Galatians! Who put a spell on you — you, in front of whom Jesus Christ crucified was pictured so plainly?
Just answer me this: did you receive the Spirit by keeping the law, or by hearing and believing?
Are you really that senseless? Having started in the Spirit, are you now trying to finish by your own effort?
Did you go through so much for nothing — if it really was for nothing?
Does God supply the Spirit and work miracles among you because you keep the law, or because you hear and believe?
Consider Abraham: he trusted God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.
So understand: it's those who live by faith who are truly Abraham's children.
Scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the nations by faith, announced the good news ahead of time to Abraham: 'through you all nations will be blessed.'
So those who live by faith are blessed together with Abraham, the man of faith.
Everyone who relies on keeping the law is under a curse, since it's written: cursed is everyone who doesn't keep doing everything written in the book of the law.
Clearly no one is justified before God by the law, because 'the righteous will live by faith.'
But the law isn't based on faith; rather, 'whoever does these things will live by them.'
Christ bought us back from the law's curse by becoming a curse on our behalf — since it's written, cursed is everyone hung on a tree —
so that Abraham's blessing might reach the nations through Christ Jesus, and we might receive the promised Spirit through faith.
Brothers, let me put it in human terms: even a person's ratified agreement can't be canceled or added to once it's confirmed.
Now the promises were given to Abraham and to his offspring. It doesn't say 'and to offsprings,' as if meaning many, but 'and to your offspring,' meaning one — who is Christ.
Here's my point: a covenant already confirmed by God can't be voided by a law that showed up 430 years later, canceling the promise.
If the inheritance comes through the law, it no longer comes through promise; but God freely granted it to Abraham through a promise.
So what was the point of the law? It was added because of wrongdoing, until the promised offspring would arrive, arranged through angels by a mediator.
A mediator implies more than one party, but God is one.
Is the law then opposed to God's promises? Certainly not — if a law had been given able to give life, righteousness really would come from the law.
But scripture locked up the whole world under sin, so that the promise, through faith in Jesus Christ, could be given to those who believe.
Before faith came, we were kept under guard by the law, locked up until the coming faith was revealed.
So the law was like a guardian in charge of us until Christ came, so that we might be justified by faith.
Now that faith has arrived, we're no longer under that guardian.
You are all children of God through faith in Christ Jesus.
All of you who were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ.
There's no longer Jew or Greek, slave or free, male or female — you are all one in Christ Jesus.
And if you belong to Christ, then you're Abraham's offspring, heirs according to the promise.
